items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 20:1
items.html: Four aspects of thirteen are discerned in the head of Arich Anpin: first, the thirteen of the Galgalta, which are revealed in the forehead and in the face, as written on Page 339, Item 96. Second, the thirteen white paths. Third, the thirteen strands of hair. Fourth, the thirteen corrections of the beard. As the Rav continues there in Items 105, 106, etc. Now, the thirteen white hairs are attributed to the Galgalta, because they are clothed in the head of the Galgalta. And the thirteen strands of hair are attributed to Mocha deAvira, because the hairs are restrictions whose beginning starts only at the membrane of the Avir, where the power of the screen of the second restriction operates; by reason of it the Mochin were corrected with the MEM-LAMED-TZADIK of Tzelem, and the Galgalta does not receive the first three of Hochma that it deserves to receive from the stature of AB, for the MEM of Tzelem does not receive into itself anything but concealed Hassadim, in the secret of 'for He delights in mercy,' as is the nature of the first three of Bina, as is known. Hence that part of the first three of AB goes out of the head and is concealed in the secret of a returning surrounding light, and the reflected lights and garments of these first three of AB are called hairs, as is known. Thus all the going out of the AB outside, and the hairs that were made in the aspect of the waste of the brain, all come from the power of the correction of the membrane of the Avir. Therefore the hairs are attributed to Mocha deAvira — that is, from the aspect of the membrane with which it was corrected. And the thirteen corrections of the beard are attributed to the Sealed Brain, for the hairs too received the correction of Tzelem, in which the MEM within them was received upon the Galgalta in the aspect of pure wool; but the LAMED-TZADIK within them, which are not fit to attach to the Galgalta (which is the aspect of MEM), come out of the aspect of the head of the Galgalta and receive only the illumination of the Sealed Brain. For in the place of the head, the illumination of the Sealed Brain cannot be revealed, since the Galgalta, which is higher than it, illuminates there, and the illumination of the Sealed Brain does not ascend there in name; rather, in the place where the illumination of the Galgalta ends, there the illumination of the Sealed Brain begins. And since the LAMED-TZADIK of the hairs — which are the thirteen corrections of the beard — cannot receive from the Galgalta, as above, therefore the illumination of the Sealed Brain is revealed in them, and hence the thirteen corrections of the beard are attributed to the Sealed Brain.
